answer.exemplar: Automatic registration removes a step, since an eligible person who renews a licence no longer has to choose registration in person, so young adults, movers and people who drive but never visit a register office get enrolled; it also prevents rejected ballots by keeping the list current after moves. Against that, updates now run automatically, so stale name and address records are dropped sooner, and eligible citizens who lack documents or a stable address can fall off faster than before, a change in who is registered rather than only in how many.

questions.explanation: A strong answer separates the two channels that raise turnout, lower effort to register and fewer stale records causing rejected ballots, from the distributional risk that automatic purges remove eligible voters faster who lack stable documents. Naming only the benefit, or only the risk, misses the tradeoff the reform creates.
